facts.raw_span: crusting, irritation, and recurrent sinus infections for the past 5 years
denied hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
no prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma were reported
occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water
destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, along with purulent, yellow drainage and crusting
C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, white blood cell count, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel results were normal
HIV test was negative
substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate
thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses, erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system
enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum
sinus mucosa showed noncaseating granulomas
AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node was positive

concepts.why: The presence of noncaseating granulomas, destruction of the septal cartilage and turbinates, and erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system support this diagnosis
The presence of noncaseating granulomas and enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum support this diagnosis
The presence of purulent, yellow drainage and crusting, and recurrent sinus infections support this diagnosis
The positive AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node supports this diagnosis
The presence of erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system and enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum support this diagnosis
The presence of purulent, yellow drainage and crusting, and growth of Staphylococcus aureus support this diagnosis
The presence of purulent, yellow drainage and crusting, and growth of Pseudomonas support this diagnosis
The presence of recurrent sinus infections and negative HIV test support this diagnosis
The presence of erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system and enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum support this diagnosis
The presence of noncaseating granulomas supports this diagnosis
The substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate is consistent with the destructive nature of Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis.

rationales.F01: Recurrent sinus infections suggest chronic sinusitis or granulomatous disease
rationales.F05: Destruction of septal cartilage and turbinates is consistent with granulomatous disease or chronic sinusitis
rationales.F10: Enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum could indicate granulomatous disease or tuberculosis
rationales.F11: Noncaseating granulomas are characteristic of sarcoidosis or granulomatous disease
rationales.F12: Positive AFB PCR probe is diagnostic for tuberculosis

frontier_selector.rationale: AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node was positive and second FESS AFB PCR probe was positive, which are strong evidence for tuberculosis, despite the patient's HIV test being negative.
